title: SSC CPO Paper-1 Full Length Mock Test 06 (Hard Level)
description: Hard Level Full Length Mock Test for SSC CPO SI Paper-1. 100 Questions | 60 Minutes | Reasoning 25, GA 25, Quant 25, English 25.
instructions: Yeh Hard Level Full Length Mock Test hai.
Total 100 questions: General Intelligence & Reasoning 25, General Knowledge & GA 25, Quantitative Aptitude 25, English Comprehension 25.
Har question 1 mark ka hai. Galat jawab par 0.25 marks katenge.
SSC CPO SI Paper-1 latest pattern ke anusar (condensed 100Q mock).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Architect : Blueprint :: Composer : ?
questions.explanation: Architect designs a blueprint; a composer designs a musical score.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing term: 3, 8, 18, 38, 78, ?
questions.explanation: Each term = previous×2 + 2: 78×2+2=158.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: If POLICY is written as QNMDJZ, how is MARKET written?
questions.explanation: Each letter is increased by 1: M→N, A→B, R→S, K→L, E→F, T→U giving NBSLFU.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, 'She is the daughter of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the girl related to the man?
questions.explanation: Only son of grandfather is the man's father; father's daughter is sister (or himself if male). Girl is sister.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: A man walks 10 km North, turns right 6 km, turns right 10 km, then left 4 km. How far and in which direction from start?
questions.explanation: After 10N, 6E, 10S he is 6E of start, then left (from south-facing after second right? Start N, right faces E, right faces S, left from S is E so +4E = 10 km East.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All medals are trophies. Some trophies are prizes. Conclusions: I. Some medals are prizes. II. No medal is a prize.
questions.explanation: Some trophies prizes does not force medals to be prizes; I and II form complementary pair (either-or).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: P ≥ Q = R > S ≤ T. Which is definitely true?
questions.explanation: P ≥ Q = R > S ⇒ P > S is certain.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Five friends A B C D E sit in a row facing North. C is second to the left of E. A is at an extreme end. B is immediate right of A. Who sits in the middle?
questions.explanation: A B _ _ _ and C second left of E. Possible A B C D E so middle D; or A B D C E middle D.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: If the word FORCE is seen in a mirror placed vertically to the right, the last letter of the image appears as?
questions.explanation: Vertical mirror reverses left-right; last visible letter of image corresponds to reversed first letter wait: FORCE reversed as ECROF so first of image is E (mirrored glyph).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: A square paper is folded in half twice and a hole is punched at the centre of the small square. How many holes when unfolded?
questions.explanation: Two folds give 4 layers; one punch → 4 holes.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Which diagram best represents Police, Women, Mothers?
questions.explanation: Some women are police; all mothers who are women sit inside women.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: If 15 August 2023 was Tuesday, what day was 15 August 2024?
questions.explanation: 2024 is leap year and 15 Aug is after Feb 29, so +2 weekdays → Thursday.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: At what time between 4 and 5 are the hands at right angle?
options: Both A and a later time
questions.explanation: Hands are at right angle at 4 : 38 2/11 minutes (and also 4 : 21 9/11).

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Statement: The government has increased petrol prices. Conclusions: I. Demand will fall. II. Inflation may rise.
questions.explanation: Price rise of fuel commonly feeds inflation; demand fall is not certain.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Choose the odd one: 121, 144, 169, 196, 225, 256, 289
questions.explanation: All given numbers are perfect squares from 11^2 to 17^2. 256 = 16^2 = 2^8 is the only power of 2, so it is the odd one out.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Maximum number of triangles in a figure of a large triangle divided by joining midpoints and all vertices to centre (standard 3 medians)?
questions.explanation: Three medians divide a triangle into 6 small triangles plus combinations totalling 16 commonly in SSC figures of this type.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Eight persons sit around a circular table facing centre. A sits second to the left of B. C is opposite A. Who sits opposite B?
questions.explanation: Opposite of B is the person sitting opposite; with A second left of B and C opposite A, opposite B is two seats from C — uniquely determined as the person second to the right of C. Option 1.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: What is the code for 'bank'? I. 'public sector bank' is coded 'sx vt qm'. II. 'reserve bank india' is coded 'qm lp az'.
questions.explanation: From both, 'bank' is the common word and 'qm' the common code.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: If the first and third letters of the word IMPUDENT are interchanged, then 2nd and 4th, and so on, which letter is 5th from right in the new word?
questions.explanation: Pairs swap: PMIU EDNT → PMIUEDNT. 5th from right is U.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: Statement: 'Use our helmets — ride safe.' Assumptions: I. People want safety. II. Helmets reduce risk.
questions.explanation: Advertisement assumes desire for safety and efficacy of helmets.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: A machine rearranges: '49 13 72 25 8 61' step1 '8 13 72 25 49 61' (smallest to left, largest? 49 moved). If each step swaps next smallest to next left, step 2?
questions.explanation: Selection-sort like: after placing 8, next place 13 already set, then 25 to third position.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: A cube is painted red on all faces and cut into 64 small cubes. How many have exactly two faces painted?
questions.explanation: 4×4×4 cube: edges 12×2=24 small cubes with two faces painted.

questions.subject: Reasoning
questions.question: If only route from P to R is via Q and Q is closed, then
options: P can reach R another way
questions.explanation: Only route via Q and Q closed ⇒ P cannot reach R.
